title: Distant key reuse and ciphertext autokeys
question: Do fixed shifted or reflected key-reuse laws, or LP2 ciphertext used as its own key, produce a calibrated whole-lag or reused-stretch signal?
reader_question: Could a key or ciphertext segment repeat elsewhere in LP2?
summary: Amended-source replay of two complete forward/reverse lag searches finds no +30 detection under either declared model, with original controls and null gates passing.
finding: After correcting only an original one-row control-array allocation in memory, all six AC/AD source result tables reproduce byte-for-byte. AC's best whole-lag, forward-stretch and reverse-stretch scores are +7.05, +19.86 and +18.23; AD's are +5.30, +22.49 and +23.16. All are below +30. AD's +5.30 whole-lag maximum has only 14 pair opportunities and an absolute +17.41 ceiling, so cannot pass at any key. The 138 AC and 184 AD planted-control rows match; both four-null gates are valid. Source/site GP29 text agrees across 12,956 positions, with selected pair-law scores independently recomputed.
limitations: The source programs cannot run unchanged: both crash in one-row reuse controls. The in-memory shape correction is disclosed and all original tables must match before accepting a result. AC's whole-lag exclusions are calibrated only through gap 12,500 and its all-cell reused-stretch detection only from 3,000 runes; AD's corresponding bounds are 12,900 and 200. The AD maximum whole-lag score comes from an underpowered 14-pair tail. Other pair laws, word resets, changing keys, language models or later decoding layers remain untested.
next_steps: A related proposal should state the exact pair relation, gap or stretch geometry and expected full output before testing, with a planted control at the claimed length.

scope.representation: The source's continuous 12,956 GP29 rune values for LP2-00–55, verified identical to the site page transcription.
scope.procedure: Repair only AC's one-row control cumsum allocation in memory. Reproduce AC and AD full original planted-control grids, four anti-doublet null streams each, all forward lags 11 through N−11 and all eligible reverse anti-diagonals. AC tests three pair laws ×29 shifts; AD tests four ×29. Compare every generated lag, top and control TSV byte with the pinned source; independently recompute representative scores.
scope.parameters: AC: 12,935 forward lags, 3 relations, 29 shifts, 138 control rows, Pmax 12,500/Mmin 3,000. AD: same 12,935 lag rows, 4 relations, 29 shifts, 184 control rows, Pmax 12,900/Mmin 200. Fixed +30 positive line and −10 calibrated exclusion line; four null streams per stage. Source-provided control draws and seeds retained.
scope.exclusions: Different text layers, page/word resets, lag under 11, other pair laws or plaintext priors, adaptive shifts, keys with nonlinear evolution, and reused stretches shorter than each calibrated control bound.

review.kind: pinned public-source AC/AD replay with disclosed one-line runtime repair and independent pair-score checks
review.reviewer: All six pinned tables and 322 planted-control rows reproduced byte-for-byte after in-memory source shape fix; two four-null validity gates passed; site runes and sampled source F/S scores independently checked

reproduction.environment: Python 3 and NumPy. The full amended-source replay additionally needs the pinned external Wulfic checkout at the stated commit.

visuals.caption: Best whole-lag and stretch scores from both source models, each below the +30 pass line. Source control power is bounded by tested gap and stretch lengths.
